matrix.label: matrix
matrix.short: A rectangular array of numbers that can encode a linear transformation, data table, or system of coefficients.

visual.note: Click a row or column to see how a matrix is organized.

vector.label: vector
vector.short: An ordered list of numbers. Geometrically, a vector can represent a direction and magnitude.

linear-transformation.label: linear transformation
linear-transformation.short: A rule that preserves vector addition and scalar multiplication. Matrices are the coordinate representation of linear transformations.

composition.label: composition
composition.short: Applying transformations in sequence. In ABCx, C acts first, then B, then A.

decomposition.label: decomposition
decomposition.short: Rewriting one matrix as structured factors or pieces whose properties make the original matrix easier to understand or compute with.

rank.label: rank
rank.short: The number of independent directions carried by a matrix; equivalently, the dimension of its column space (or row space).

visual.note: The third column equals the first plus the second, so it adds no new direction: rank = 2.

column-space.label: column space
column-space.short: All linear combinations of the columns of a matrix. Its dimension is the matrix rank.

null-space.label: null space
null-space.short: All input vectors x that are sent to zero: Ax = 0.

basis.label: basis
basis.short: A minimal independent set of vectors that can generate every vector in a space by linear combination.

orthogonal.label: orthogonal
orthogonal.short: Perpendicular in the inner-product sense. For vectors u and v, orthogonal means uᵀv = 0.

orthonormal.label: orthonormal
orthonormal.short: Orthogonal and unit length at the same time. An orthonormal matrix preserves lengths and angles.

unitary.label: unitary
unitary.short: The complex-number analogue of an orthogonal matrix: Q*Q = I.

diagonal.label: diagonal matrix
diagonal.short: A matrix whose only potentially nonzero entries lie on the main diagonal. In SVD, Σ is allowed to be rectangular diagonal.

triangular.label: triangular matrix
triangular.short: A square matrix with zeros entirely above or below the main diagonal.

transpose.label: transpose
transpose.short: Swap rows and columns. The transpose of A is written Aᵀ.

conjugate-transpose.label: conjugate transpose
conjugate-transpose.short: For complex matrices: transpose and then complex-conjugate every entry. For real matrices it reduces to the ordinary transpose.

hermitian.label: Hermitian
hermitian.short: A complex square matrix equal to its conjugate transpose: W = W*. Hermitian matrices have real eigenvalues and orthonormal eigenvectors.

eigenvector.label: eigenvector
eigenvector.short: A nonzero direction that a square matrix only scales: Av = λv.

eigenvalue.label: eigenvalue
eigenvalue.short: The scaling λ associated with an eigenvector in Av = λv.

spectral-theorem.label: spectral theorem
spectral-theorem.short: Every real symmetric / complex Hermitian matrix has an orthonormal eigenbasis, so it can be diagonalized by an orthogonal/unitary change of basis.

singular-value.label: singular value
singular-value.short: A nonnegative scaling strength σᵢ in SVD. Larger σᵢ means that singular direction contributes more to the transformation.

right-singular-vector.label: right singular vector
right-singular-vector.short: A special input direction vᵢ. SVD maps it according to Avᵢ = σᵢuᵢ.

left-singular-vector.label: left singular vector
left-singular-vector.short: The corresponding output direction uᵢ in Avᵢ = σᵢuᵢ.

outer-product.label: outer product
outer-product.short: For column vectors u and v, uvᵀ is a matrix. If both are nonzero, this matrix has rank 1.

frobenius-norm.label: Frobenius norm
frobenius-norm.short: The square root of the sum of the squares of every matrix entry. It is a natural Euclidean distance between matrices.

low-rank-approximation.label: low-rank approximation
low-rank-approximation.short: Approximating a matrix using fewer independent directions than the original matrix.

truncated-svd.label: truncated SVD
truncated-svd.short: Keep only the largest k singular values and their singular vectors to obtain a rank-k approximation.

pca.label: PCA
pca.short: A dimensionality-reduction method that finds orthogonal directions of maximum variance in centered data. Through SVD, these are the right singular vectors of the centered data matrix.

principal-component.label: principal component
principal-component.short: An orthogonal direction along which centered data has maximal remaining variance.

variance.label: variance
variance.short: A measure of spread. In PCA, squared singular values (with covariance scaling) determine how much variance each principal component explains.

covariance.label: covariance matrix
covariance.short: A matrix describing how centered features vary together. PCA eigenvectors are eigenvectors of the covariance matrix.

full-svd.label: full SVD
full-svd.short: The version A = UΣVᵀ where U and V are square orthogonal matrices and Σ has the same rectangular shape as A.

condensed-svd.label: condensed SVD
condensed-svd.short: An SVD that keeps only columns associated with the nonzero (or needed) singular values, avoiding unnecessary zero directions.

interactives.title: Matrix Composition as Sequential Transformations
interactives.instruction: The product ABC acts on x from right to left: C transforms the input first, followed by B and A.

interactives.title: Matrix Factorization Methods
interactives.instruction: Five factorizations represent the same matrix through different structures, with each set of factors providing a route to reconstruct A.

items.name: LU

factors.label: L
factors.role: Lower triangular: it stores the elimination multipliers.

factors.label: U
factors.role: Upper triangular: this is the simplified matrix left by elimination.

items.why: LU turns Gaussian elimination into reusable matrix factors.

items.name: QR

factors.label: R
factors.role: R stores the coordinates in that orthonormal basis and is upper triangular.

items.why: QR separates clean directions from the coefficients needed to rebuild the original columns.

items.name: Cholesky

factors.label: Lᵀ
factors.role: The transpose mirrors L because A is symmetric positive definite.

items.why: Cholesky uses symmetry and positive definiteness so one triangular factor is enough.

items.name: Spectral

factors.label: Q
factors.role: Columns are orthonormal eigenvectors: the new coordinate axes.

factors.label: Λ
factors.role: Diagonal eigenvalues: pure scaling along the eigenvector directions.

factors.label: Qᵀ
factors.role: Returns from eigen-coordinates to the original coordinates.

items.why: A symmetric matrix becomes pure independent scaling when viewed in its eigenbasis.

items.name: SVD

factors.label: Σ
factors.role: Nonnegative singular values: independent scaling strengths.

items.why: SVD works for every matrix and isolates the transformation into analyze → scale → orient.

interactives.title: Vector Transformation under the SVD
interactives.instruction: The factorization separates a vector transformation into an orthogonal change of coordinates by Vᵀ, scaling by Σ, and reorientation by U.

interactives.title: Geometric Action of the SVD
interactives.instruction: Vᵀ re-expresses the unit circle in a new orthogonal basis, Σ stretches it into an ellipse, and U sets its final orientation; the singular values determine the axis lengths.

interactives.title: Existence of the Singular Value Decomposition
interactives.instruction: A rectangular matrix is embedded in a larger Hermitian matrix; the spectral theorem then yields the orthogonal singular-vector pairs that form its SVD.

interactives.title: A Matrix as a Sum of Rank-One Terms
interactives.instruction: The matrix A is expressed as a sum of rank-one terms σᵢuᵢvᵢᵀ. Adding terms successively improves the reconstruction and reduces the residual.

interactives.title: Low-Rank Reconstruction
interactives.instruction: The original matrix A, its rank-k approximation Aₖ, and the residual A − Aₖ share one color scale. Increasing k improves the approximation and reduces the Frobenius error.

interactives.title: Singular Spectrum and Rank Selection
interactives.instruction: The ordered singular values show dominant components followed by a sharp decline. Retained energy and Frobenius reconstruction error vary with the selected rank k.

interactives.title: PCA Projection onto the First Principal Component
interactives.instruction: Observations are projected orthogonally onto PC₁, which explains 99.2% of the variance in this example; perpendicular displacement represents the residual.

interactives.title: Low-Rank Image Reconstruction Using the SVD
interactives.instruction: Rank-k reconstructions recover the image’s broad structure before finer detail. Four nonzero singular values suffice for an exact reconstruction of this 18 × 18 example, while lower ranks require fewer stored values.

interactives.title: Low-Rank Factorization of a Neural-Network Layer
interactives.instruction: A dense weight matrix W is approximated by UₖΣₖVₖᵀ, replacing one large linear transformation with two narrower transformations.

interactives.title: Conceptual Map of SVD and Its Applications
interactives.instruction: The map connects matrix composition, factorization, rank, truncated SVD, PCA, image reconstruction, and low-rank neural-network layers.
